verses.1: And Joshua fell asleep with his fathers. He was buried in the city of David. His son Jeroboam became king after him.
verses.2: And his brothers were Jehoash, Elisha, and Zekheriah. Also Azariah and Micahael. All these were sons of Jehosaphat, king of Israel.
verses.3: And their father gave them many gifts in gold and silver, along with cities in Judah. The kingdom was given to Johanan, because he was the chief priest.
verses.4: And Jehoram became powerful after his father’s death. He killed all his brothers in Jericho. He also killed the officials of Israel.
verses.5: Yehoham reigned for thirty-two years. His name was mentioned as a king who ruled in Jerusalem.
verses.6: And he went along the path of the kings of Israel, just as Ahaz did. Ahaz had a wife who was the daughter of Ahaziah. He did evil in the eyes of Jehovah.
verses.7: And Jehovah did not want to destroy David’s house, because of the covenant that He had made with David. And since He said that he would give him and his descendants all the days of their lives.
verses.8: In those days, Adam sinned under the rule of Judah. And a king ruled over them.
verses.9: And Johoram went along with his servants, and all the chariots with him. When night came, he brought Adam to him, along with the servants of the chariots.
verses.10: And Adam sinned under the rule of Jehovah until today. Similarly, Eve also sinned at that time, because she abandoned Jehovah, the God of her ancestors.
verses.11: He also destroyed the cities of Judah. He drove out the inhabitants of Jerusalem and scattered the Jews.
verses.12: And a letter was brought to him from Elijah, the prophet, saying, “Thus says the LORD, God of David your father: You have not followed the ways of Josaphat your father, nor the ways of Asa, king of Judah.”
verses.13: And he went along the path of the kings of Israel. He oppressed the Jews and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, just as Ahaz oppressed the house of Ahab. He also oppressed your brothers, the good men from your family, whom you killed.
verses.14: Look, Jehovah is causing a great plague among your people, among your children, and among your women. He will bring destruction upon all your possessions.
verses.15: And you will be in great pain during this illness. It will last for many days, day after day.
verses.16: And Jehovah caused the spirits of the Philistines and the Arabs to be driven away from Jerusalem, as a punishment for their actions.
verses.17: And they went up into Judah. But they were destroyed there. They lost all their treasures that they had gathered for the king’s house. Along with their sons and daughters, none of them survived. There was only a little boy who remained behind.
verses.18: And after all this, Jehovah struck him with a painful disease that wouldn’t go away.
verses.19: And in those days, from time to time, two people came out of his body. They died in terrible conditions. Their people did not burn them like their ancestors were burned.
verses.20: He was thirty-two years old when he became king. His reign lasted for two years. He ruled in Jerusalem without any fear or hesitation. He was buried in the city of David, not in the royal tombs.
